error.title: Something went wrong
error.description: The interface hit an unexpected error. Your display was not changed.

more.title: More
more.subtitle: Language, updates and information about VRes.

updates.title: Updates
updates.description: VRes checks GitHub for new versions. It's the only internet connection it makes.
updates.onlyInApp: Only available in the installed app.

safety.title: If something looks wrong
safety.description: When you close VRes, your display goes back to how it was. The Ctrl + Alt + Shift + R shortcut resets it at any time, even with the window closed, just like “Reset display” in the tray.

about.title: About
about.license: Free software under the GPL-3.0 license. No account and no telemetry.

startup.title: Startup
startup.description: VRes starts with Windows straight to the tray, without opening the window, and applies your last look.
startup.label: Start with Windows

behavior.title: When closing the window
behavior.description: VRes can stay in the tray or quit completely.
behavior.closeQuits: Closing the window will quit VRes and your display will go back to normal.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostic report
diagnostics.description: To attach to a bug report. It doesn't include your user name or your PC's name, and VRes doesn't send it: you copy it and paste it wherever you want.

licenses.title: Licenses
licenses.description: VRes is free software (GPL-3.0). These are the licenses of what it uses.

reset.title: Reset everything
reset.description: Brings VRes back to how it was when installed.
reset.confirm: Your saved looks and crosshairs, profiles and added games, hotkeys, Dark Boost and Zoom, theme and background are deleted, and the look goes back to neutral. This can't be undone.
reset.done: Done: VRes is like freshly installed.

display.title: Display
display.subtitle: Saturation and fine color tuning, monitor by monitor.
display.compareHint: Hold to see the original image
display.resetHint: Sets every value back to neutral

targets.title: Apply to
targets.description: Unticked monitors keep their own colors.
targets.partial: Some monitors are unticked: saturation is paused, because Windows applies it to the whole desktop at once. Fine tuning still applies to the ticked monitors.
targets.none: No monitors are ticked: changes are paused.

saturation.title: Saturation
saturation.hint: 100 is the image as it ships

fineTune.title: Fine tuning
fineTune.description: Applied per monitor, on top of each one's calibration.

display.resetParam: Double-click to go back to neutral
display.emergency: If something looks wrong: Ctrl + Alt + Shift + R resets the display at any time.
display.unavailable: The VRes engine is not available.

vibrance.title: Digital vibrance
vibrance.hint: 50 leaves vibrance as you have it in your graphics panel

depth.title: Color depth
depth.description: How each color's brightness is computed, hue shift and darkening a color.
depth.darkenAmount: How much to darken (lightens its complement)

vision.title: Color vision
vision.description: Helps tell colors apart if you have color blindness.

eyeCare.title: Eye care
eyeCare.description: Less blue and less brightness for playing at night. Adds on top of any look.

display.profileNote: A game profile is in use: while the game is in front, its look replaces this tab's.

reasons.hdrActive: HDR is on: fine tuning doesn't apply on this monitor.
reasons.partialTargets: Paused because some monitors are unticked.
reasons.exclusiveFullscreen: Game in exclusive full screen: saturation moves to the driver's vibrance, which does show there.
reasons.magConflict: Another app (for example, Magnifier or Windows color filters) is using the color filter.
reasons.rampOutOfRange: The requested curve exceeds what Windows allows: the closest one was applied.
reasons.rampRejected: Windows rejected fine tuning on this monitor.
reasons.rampConflict: Another app (Night light, f.lux, a calibrator) is changing this monitor's colors.
reasons.vibranceBackendMissing: This monitor has no driver vibrance.
reasons.vibranceApproximated: Saturation is approximated with driver vibrance.
reasons.displayGone: The display is no longer connected.
reasons.notInGame: Only works with the game in the foreground.
reasons.modeNotSupported: The monitor doesn't support that mode.
reasons.safeModeAfterCrash: Safe mode after an unexpected shutdown.
reasons.scalingIgnored: The graphics card or the monitor ignored the requested scaling: you may see black bars.
reasons.zoomUnavailable: Zoom failed (for example, with Windows Magnifier open).

notices.recovered: VRes didn't close properly last time: it already restored the original colors.
notices.safeMode: For safety, VRes started with color turned off. Turn it on whenever you like.
notices.emergencyReset: Display reset: color is now off.
notices.hotkeyTaken: Another program uses Ctrl + Alt + Shift + R, so the emergency shortcut isn't available. You can reset the display from the tray.
notices.engineUnavailable: The VRes engine couldn't start. Restart the app; if it keeps happening, please report it.
notices.modeExpired: The new resolution reverted by itself because you didn't confirm it.
notices.toggleHotkeyTaken: Another program uses the resolution hotkey you chose. Pick another one in the Resolution tab.
notices.zoomUnavailable: Zoom failed. If Windows Magnifier is open, close it and try again.
notices.crosshairHotkeyTaken: Another program uses the crosshair hotkey you chose. Pick another one in the Crosshair tab.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.subtitle: Stretched resolution, refresh rate and HDR, with automatic rollback.

current.title: Current mode
current.hdrHint: With HDR on, saturation and fine tuning aren't reliable. When you close VRes, HDR goes back to how it was.

presets.title: Stretched
presets.description: Fill the screen with a wider image. When you try one, VRes asks you to confirm it: if you don't answer, it reverts by itself.
presets.unavailable: Needs a custom resolution (coming in v1.0)
presets.none: No stretched resolutions for this display.

custom.title: Custom
custom.description: Choose width, height and refresh rate.
custom.tooLarge: It can't exceed the native resolution ({{size}}).
custom.notListed: Your monitor doesn't list that resolution: it needs a driver custom resolution (coming in v1.0).

pending.title: Keep this resolution?
pending.body: If you don't answer, it goes back to the previous one by itself.

resolved.kept: Done: {{mode}} is applied. The hotkey now toggles to this resolution.
resolved.reverted: You went back to the previous resolution.
resolved.expired: No answer: the resolution reverted by itself.

hotkey.title: Native ↔ stretched hotkey
hotkey.description: Toggles between Windows' resolution and the last stretched one you kept, without opening VRes.
hotkey.noTarget: Keep a stretched resolution to be able to use the hotkey.

issues.unknownKey: That key can't be used as a hotkey.
issues.needsModifier: Letters, numbers and symbols need Ctrl, Alt or Win.
issues.reserved: It's reserved (emergency hotkey, F12 or Escape).
issues.altGrClash: Ctrl + Alt equals AltGr on Latin American keyboards: it could stop you from typing characters like @.
issues.overlayClash: Your graphics card's overlay uses it.
issues.taken: Another program already uses that hotkey.
issues.duplicate: Another VRes hotkey already uses it.

errors.modeNotSupported: Your monitor doesn't list that resolution.
errors.modeBusy: Another resolution change is in progress: answer the pending one first.
errors.modeExpired: That change was already kept, reverted or expired.
errors.modeNotConfirmed: The hotkey only toggles to resolutions you've kept once.
errors.displayGone: That display is no longer connected.
errors.hotkeyTaken: Another program already uses that hotkey. Choose another one.
errors.crosshairInvalid: That crosshair could not be drawn.
errors.backgroundInvalid: That image won't work: it must be PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 25 MB.
errors.potatoUnavailable: There's no NVIDIA driver with game profiles.
errors.potatoCancelled: Nothing changed: you need to accept the administrator prompt.
errors.potatoFailed: The driver didn't save the change. Try again or restart the PC.

crosshair.title: Crosshair
crosshair.subtitle: Your own crosshair over any game: a transparent window on top, without touching the game.
crosshair.warning: Some games and tournaments consider an external crosshair an advantage: check their rules before using it in competitive play.

preview.title: Preview
preview.description: How it looks over the game: real size and zoomed ×4.

hotkey.title: Show/hide hotkey
hotkey.description: Shows or hides the crosshair without leaving the game. If a game profile controls it, the change lasts while that game stays in the foreground.

image.title: Custom image
image.hint: Use an image with transparency (up to 256 × 256 px).
image.invalid: That image could not be read.

placement.title: Where it shows
placement.hideHint: OBS, Discord and Windows captures don't see it; you do.

browse.title: More crosshairs
browse.description: The crosshair gallery lives on the website, so the app stays light. Copy a code and paste it below in "Share".

looks.title: Looks
looks.description: Starting points for each game, plus your own. Tune them by eye: every monitor is different.
looks.name: Name

share.notShareable: Image crosshairs don't fit in a code.
share.clamped: Some values were out of range and were adjusted.
share.lookDescription: Send it over Discord or WhatsApp as text, or paste a friend's.
share.crosshairDescription: A text code with your crosshair; paste a friend's to try it. It also takes VALORANT (0;P;…) and CS2 (CSGO-… or CS…) crosshair codes.

placeholder.crosshair: VRC1-…, or a VALORANT or CS2 code

errors.badChar: The code has characters that don't belong.
errors.badChecksum: The code was copied wrong: check it's complete.
errors.unsupportedVersion: That code is from a newer VRes: update the app.
errors.wrongKind: That code is for something else (for example, a crosshair where a look goes).
errors.imageNotShareable: Image crosshairs don't fit in a code.

share.imported: Crosshair imported from {{game}}. It's an approximation: tweak it and save it.

library.title: Library
library.subtitle: Your looks, crosshairs and resolutions, stored on your PC. No account, no servers.
library.resolutionsHint: Resolutions you kept at some point. When you apply one, VRes asks you to confirm it.
library.resolutionsEmpty: You haven't kept any stretched resolution yet.

import.title: Import a code
import.description: Paste a VRes code (look, crosshair or resolution) to save or apply it.

quick.title: Quick adjust
quick.description: Color, saturation, vibrance and looks one click away.

profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.subtitle: One profile per game: VRes applies it when it detects the game in front and goes back to yours with Alt+Tab or when you close it.
profiles.inactive: No game with a profile in front: your desktop settings are used.
profiles.resolutionHint: Only ones you've kept. Applied when the game starts, reverted when it closes.

custom.title: Add a game
custom.description: Pick an open program: VRes recognizes it by its executable name.
custom.empty: No programs with a window are open

enhancers.title: Dark Boost
enhancers.subtitle: To see better at key moments, while you hold a key or a mouse button.
enhancers.warning: Use it with care: some games and tournaments consider brightening shadows an advantage and may penalize it. Check their rules; the decision and the risk are yours.

state.waitingGame: Waiting for a game in front

scope.label: Where
scope.games: Only with a game in front

binding.label: Key or button
binding.recording: Press a key or a mouse button…
binding.hint: Esc cancels. The left button can't be used.
binding.unsupported: That key can't be used. Try another one.
binding.same: Dark Boost and Zoom use the same key: they turn on together.

darkBoost.title: Dark Boost
darkBoost.description: Brightens shadows and blacks while you use it. It also works in exclusive fullscreen (tint and invert don't).
darkBoost.invertWarning: Inverting changes every color at once: it can be uncomfortable, or dangerous if you're photosensitive. It doesn't invert with HDR on.

zoom.title: Zoom
zoom.description: Enlarges the center of the screen while you use it. It's only visual: the game and the mouse don't change.
zoom.magnifierNote: It doesn't work while Windows Magnifier is open.

home.title: Home
home.subtitle: Your main config in one place: colors, crosshair, resolution and hotkeys. It saves itself and comes back every time you open VRes.

scope.title: Where it applies
scope.description: Choose whether your main config is always on or only while you play.
scope.alwaysHint: On the desktop and in games.
scope.gamesHint: With a game in front. On the desktop, the screen stays normal and without a crosshair.
scope.pick: Tap the games where it applies:
scope.anyGame: With none selected, it applies to any game VRes recognizes (the built-in ones and those you add in Profiles).
scope.fullscreen: Also in full screen: there, saturation moves to the driver's vibrance (NVIDIA or AMD). The crosshair shows in borderless windowed and in Windows 10/11 full screen, not in old exclusive full screen.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.none: You haven't picked a stretched resolution yet. Try one in Resolution and keep it.

hotkeys.title: Hotkeys
hotkeys.description: They work with the window closed and with the game in front.

games.title: Games with their own config
games.description: A profile changes colors, crosshair or resolution only in that game.
games.none: No game has its own config yet.

potato.title: Potato graphics
potato.subtitle: Flat, detail-free textures for more FPS, on NVIDIA cards. VRes sets it in the game's driver profile, just like the NVIDIA control panel: it doesn't touch the game.
potato.warning: Use it at your own risk: some games consider lowering textures from the driver an advantage (Riot called it an “exploit” in VALORANT) and may penalize it. Check the game's rules.

unavailable.title: An NVIDIA card is required
unavailable.description: The NVIDIA driver with game profiles wasn't found. This feature isn't available on AMD or Intel.

off.name: Normal
off.hint: No changes: the game looks as usual.

low.name: Low textures
low.hint: Simpler textures and less visual noise. A bit more FPS.

potato.applying: Saving to the driver… accept the Windows prompt.
potato.restart: Done. Close and reopen the game to see it.
potato.custom: This game already had its own texture setting in the driver (for example, from Profile Inspector). Picking a level replaces it.

how.title: How it works
how.driver: It changes the textures' “LOD Bias” in the game's NVIDIA driver profile. It works in DirectX 11 games, like ROB RUN.
how.admin: The driver asks for administrator permission to save: Windows shows a prompt each time you change the level.
how.hybrid: On laptops with two GPUs, the game has to run on the NVIDIA one (Windows Settings › Display › Graphics).
how.undo: It stays saved even if you close VRes. To go back, pick “Normal”.
